Commentary.Commentary: Hello and welcome back for the chase. The Australian players have taken to the field and the two opening batsmen for West Indies, Shai Hope and Evin Lewis are at the crease. Mitchell Starc to get us underway with his steaming left-arm pace.

So then, West Indies need 188 to win and though it might seem like a sub-par total by Australia, you never know what will happen. West Indies were shot out for only 123 in the first ODI so they will have to better their last performance to scale down this target. Australia will look for a fast start with the ball. Let’s see if the chase is straightforward or there will be some tumbles. We will find out after a short break.

Akeal Hosein is up for a quick chat! The spinner says that he is pleased with his performance after not having a good T20I series. Shares that the conditions are a bit spin-friendly but still, you have to pitch the ball in the right area. Feels that partnerships will be the key as small totals can be difficult. Wants his team to take it as deep as possible.

West Indies had a dream start as their bowlers cleaned up the Australian top order in a jiffy and they weren’t finished. After Powerplay 1, Akeal Hosein emerged on the scene who just spun the ball like he never has and got three wickets with his first ten deliveries. He bowled in tandem with Hayden Walsh. Both of them continued to attack but Wade and Starc were up to the task. Finally, when Hayden Walsh came back on he broke the partnership but Zampa stayed with Wade. West Indies did manage to get Wade out but just failed to close out the innings and gave away some valuable runs which might come back to haunt them. Still, they will be the favourites given the score Australia posted.

A decent comeback by Australia after a forgetful start. They had a disastrous beginning with their top three getting sent back to the pavilion when the score was just 26. They were again rocked after Powerplay 1 by Akeal Hosein who ripped through their middle order and picked up 3 wickets, leaving Australia reeling at 45 for 6 within 13 overs. Then came Australia’s fightback with Wade and Starc adding 51 runs for the 7th wicket. Starc fell to spin as well, but Zampa came in and did a fine job. The hammer blow was dealt when Wade was dismissed for 36 runs, although it was not done yet. Wes Agar joined forces with Adam and together they stitched in a record 9th wicket partnership at this venue to hand Australia a fighting score.

OUT! Joseph picks the final wicket! He follows the batsman down the leg side with a fuller length ball, Wes Agar is looking for space to flick it on the leg side but mistimes it badly off the leading edge towards Evin Lewis in the ring. He takes a simple catch at point and AUSTRALIA ARE BOWLED OUT FOR 187!
Commentary.Howout: c Evin Lewis b Alzarri Joseph

Commentary.Commentary: The last man to come in is the debutant, Riley Meredith.

OUT! The off stump is obliterated! End of a good fighting knock by Adam Zampa. Cottrell serves a pacy length ball in the line of the stumps, Adam moves back to make room for a shot over the off side but fails to connect. The 9th wicket has gone down for 187 and that ends the record 59-run stand at this venue.
In the channel outside off, angling away, Adam walks across the stumps and tries his best to dig it out but misses.
Short and outside off, forced through point for one.
Slight width outside off, short in length, Wes swishes and misses.
Bowling change. Sheldon Cottrell comes back to replace Hayden Walsh.
Angling a length ball outside off, Agar backs away a too much and then has to leave.
SIX! Agar is opening his arms! A length delivery outside off, Wes stands back and rifles it over wide long off for a biggie.
Fuller on off, this is driven through the covers for a single.
The batsman has just blocked that from his crease.
A gentle push to covers for a single.
Fuller on middle, knocked down to long on for one. 50-run stand comes up!
SIX! Agar goes big! Full and outside off, Agar walks across and swings it over square leg for a biggie.
FOUR! Holder attempts for a yorker but it turns out to be a very full ball in the slot, Agar drills it down the ground and finds the fence at long off.
A bit shorter on off, played towards the cover region.
FOUR! Cleverly done by Zampa. Tossed up delivery on off stump and Zampa just reverses it fine of short third man for a boundary.
Fuller this time around off and the ball is driven through cover for one.
Tossed up on off, nicely driven through covers by Zampa for a single.
Tossed up outside off and Agar fetches this one and sweeps it uppishly down to deep mid-wicket for a run.
Dragged down outside off, played towards the cover region.
Hayden Walsh is back on to bowl his final over.
Low full toss on off, driven straight to mid off.
Length ball on off, blocked back by Zampa.
FOUR! Short ball again and Zampa looks to hoick it over mid-wicket but gets the top-edge behind and into the fine leg fence. He won't mind it.
Back of a length on leg stump, tucked to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Length this time outside off, Zampa plays it through point into the deep for one.
A short delivery around off, Zampa safely defends it towards point by getting right behind it.
Jason Holder is back into the attack. 1/22 in his 5 overs so far.
Shortish ball, bowled on middle coming into the body, nicely fended off by Agar to the off side.
Back of a length on off, angling in, nudged to backward point by Agar.
Length ball pushed wide, Agar looks to slash but misses the ball.
Length ball outside off, played towards point.
Back of a length delivery, bowled into the deck around off. Agar swats it back past the bowler for a couple.
Full around off, driven towards the cover region.
Loopy and full on middle, Zampa tries to slog sweep but gets an under-edge on the back leg.
Quicker and shorter on off, Zampa cuts it from the back foot but finds point.
Loopy and full on off, spinning away, Zampa leaves it.
Short and outside off, Zampa lofts it with the spin over covers for two.
Spinning away from the batsman, Adam plays it down to covers.
Short and on middle, pulled over mid-wicket for one. Australia have crawled their way to 150.
Hayden Walsh is back on.
Length again and played off the back foot towards cover again for one.
Back of a length, punched off the back foot through covers for a couple.
FOUR! Fuller on off and driven towards cover, Cottrell makes a meal of it and the ball goes into the boundary.
Pitched up around off, sliced over covers into the deep for a couple by Agar.
A bit fuller and nicely defended.
Powerplay 3 time. One extra fielder, i.e. 5 can now be put outside the 30-yard circle till the end of this inning.
Length ball on the stumps, blocked back by Agar.
Good length ball on middle and off, at 141 kph, Wes pushes inside the line and edges it wide of backward point for one.
Gets behind the line of this delivery and blocks safely to the off side.
FOUR! Pulled away bravely! Sheldon Cottrell digs in a short ball around off, at 139 kph, Agar just takes his front foot out of the way and swats it over mid-wicket.
Follows the batsman down the leg side by angling in a length delivery, at 139 kph, Wes defends it with a straight blade.
Sheldon steams in from 'round the wicket and spears in a very full ball on leg at 135 kph, Wes digs it out to covers.
Goes very full, on middle at 133 kph, Agar pushes it down to mid off.
Bowling change. Sheldon Cottrell comes back into the attack.
FOUR! Lovely shot! Full and outside off, Zampa lifts it over the jumping cover fielder for a boundary. Moves to 23, his best score in this format.
Short again, outside off, Agar cuts it down to third man for a run.
JUST OVER POORAN! Joseph bangs in a short ball on middle, Zampa tries to pull but doesn't get enough bat on it. It flies towards backward square leg and beats the leaping fielder. A single taken.
Short in length and on off, Wes guides it down to third man and takes a single.
Angling in around off, the batsman has just blocked that from his crease.
Who will come in at number 10? It's going to be Wes Agar.

OUT! Wade is crestfallen, down on his one knee, cannot believe what he has done!!! Joseph fires across a fuller length ball outside off, Wade attacks it with all his might, aiming to go big over covers but the elevation is absent. It goes flat and straight into the hands of Pooran who is standing at the edge of the circle at extra cover. Can Australia reach 150 now?
Commentary.Howout: c Nicholas Pooran b Alzarri Joseph

Commentary.Commentary: Quicker off spinner on middle and leg, Zampa tries to flick but misses. Another tidy over from the part-timer!
A touch short and on off, turning back in, Adam goes back and punches it to covers.
Wide! Turning down the leg side, Zampa tries sweeping but fails to connect.
Shout for an lbw! Spinning too much. Full and on off, Zampa tries to defend but misses and is pinged on the front pad. They put in an unsuccessful appeal.
Superb delivery, floated and on middle, turning towards off, Wade fails to flick and it goes off his thigh pad to short third man. A leg bye is picked.
Fires in a flat ball on middle, Wade is hurried into his back foot defense.

Swing and a miss! Jason delivers it with a round-arm action and gets it to spin away after landing outside off, Wade tries to slog sweep but misses. Shai breaks the stumps without collecting the ball.
Too full in length and around middle, Zampa flicks but finds Pollard who is standing near the surface, you can call it a deepish forward short leg position.
Spears a length ball on middle, 138 kph, this time again Zampa hangs back to defend it towards mid-wicket.
Fuller in length and on off, angling in at 136 kph, Zampa keeps it out from the inner half of his bat to mid on.
Fires in a full ball on middle and leg, Zampa defends it to short mid-wicket.
Good length ball on middle and leg, Wade walks across and tickles it behind square leg for one.
Starts his new spell with a fuller length ball outside off, Wade drives but finds the fielder inside the ring at covers.
Bowling change. Alzarri Joseph comes back into the attack, replacing Akeal Hosein who is done with his 10 overs.
Quicker one, full and down the leg side, swept behind square leg for two. The stand moves to 29.
That is defended solidly off the front foot.
Tossed up ball on off, turning in, Adam leans forward this time in defense.
Turning back in from around off, Adam goes on the back foot in defense.
Drags his length short again and bowls it outside off, Zampa cuts but finds point.
Short and wide outside off, punched to deep cover for a single.
Jason Mohammed to continue...
SO CLOSE! Floated up nicely around off, Zampa lets it go but the ball doesn't turn and just goes over the off stump. End of a terrific spell from Akeal Hosein, 10-0-30-3.
Flighted outside off, Zampa drives it to silly point.
Fuller one on middle and leg, flicked through mid-wicket against the spin for a couple.
Tossed up on off, pushed to the cover region.
A bit flatter, drifting in on middle, defended nicely by Zampa.
Flighted on off, driven to the cover region.
Fuller and straighter this time, Wade reverses again and this time gets it to short third man.
Lucky escape for Wade! Tossed up nicely around off, slightly fuller and Wade looks to reverse but misses. The ball just misses the off pole by a whisker.
Tossed up on the stumps, flicked to deep mid-wicket for a single.
A flatter delivery on middle, Zampa defends it off the front foot.
Slightly tossed up on off, nicely driven through point by Wade for three runs. Excellent running!
Short ball outside off, punched to the cover region.
Tossed up on off, squeezed to backward point.
BEAUTY! Hosein bowls this one a touch short around off and the ball spins away sharply. Zampa, who looked to play at it, gets beaten all ends up.
Pitched up again on middle, driven towards the cover region.
Fuller on off, driven straight to point.
Flighted on off, blocked out by Zampa.
SAFE! Nicely tossed up around off, spinning away from Zampa who looks to drive. The ball takes the outside edge and goes wide of first slip for a couple.
Akeal Hosein is back on. 8-0-26-3 are his figures so far.
Shorter one on off, Zampa makes room and drives it to deep point for a single.
Flighted delivery, very full on off, pushed to long off for a run.
Tossed up around middle, Wade pushes this one gently on the off side.
Wade punches the short ball off the back foot through covers for a couple of runs.
Gives it some air this time and bowls it around off, Wade nudges it to short third man.
Full on middle, just turning away, blocked out by Wade.
Bowling change. Jason Mohammed is into the attack as the sixth bowling option. A slip in place.
A tad shorter on middle, spinning in and Wade taps it on the off side off his back foot for a quick single.
Fuller deliver on middle, Zampa sweeps it nicely to wide of fine leg for a single.
FOUR! Overpitched around off, Zampa leans into his drive and plays it through extra cover, the ball slowly but surely trickles into the fence.
Tossed up around middle and Wade pushes it towards cover for one.
Length ball on off, Wade nudges it to short third man by giving himself some room.
This one is bowled flatter and wider, Wade pulls out of his cut shot at the last moment.
Flatter ball, on off and turning in, Wade moves back and forces it off the inside part of his bat to long on. A single and Wade retains strike.
Tossed up ball on off, 81 kph, Wade gets forward and across to flick but misses. It goes off his pads to short fine leg.
Slower through the air, full and flighted on off, Wade gets forward and defends it to the off side.
Quicker one, full and on off, Adam gets forward and drives it to long off for a single.
Tossed up ball on off, the batsman has just blocked that from his crease.
Superb delivery! Just look at that. Flatter one, landing on off and spinning square, Zampa stands there like a dead duck, tries to defend but it zips past the outside edge.

DRINKS BREAK! Australia fought back well and Wade along with Starc steered the ship with a 50 plus stand but that partnership was eventually broken. Wade is still at the crease but is running out of support from the other end. West Indies looked in control but then got frustrated a bit but are now back in control.
Slower through the air, full and on middle, Wade lunges and defends it with his bat in front of the pads.
Fuller and wider outside off, Zampa reaches out and strokes it down to long off for one.
Loopy leg spinner on middle, fuller in length, Zampa gets forward and defends it to covers.
Tossed up ball on off, a bit on the shorter side, Adam pushes it from the back foot to point.
Loopy full ball on middle, Wade leans forward and wrists it in front of square leg for one. 100 up for Australia.
Walsh bowls it flatter and shorter outside off, Wade stays back and allows it through.
Quicker, fuller, on middle, Zampa defends it back to the bowler off the inner half of his bat.
Fires in a full toss on middle, Zampa chips his flick shot to deep mid-wicket for two.
Full and floated on off, pushed firmly off the front foot to covers.
Uppish but just out of the grasp of Pollard at silly point. Flatter delivery, around middle and skidding in, Zampa gets back to defend but it takes the gloves and flies past the close-in fielder.
Quicker through the air, shortish and on middle, defended from the back foot to the off side.
Flatter ball, a touch short and on off, Zampa stays back and pushes it to cover-point.
Bowling change. Akeal Hosein, the star man toady, is brought back in to put pressure on the new man.
A tossed up ball outside off, another googly, Zampa tries to drive but edges it past the stumps. Surprisingly, Wade takes a single. Zampa will be on strike for the next over.
Flighted and full on off, Zampa is forward in defense.
A googly around off, Zampa tries to defend and possibly gets sone inside edge onto the pads.
Who will come in next? It's Adam Zampa.

Review for LBW. The West Indies players thought long and hard about it but finally, Pollard decides to take the review as breaking this partnership is crucial. There is certainly no bat involved as ULTRA EDGE shows. BALL TRACKING shows three reds and the review is successful! Starc was riding his luck a bit and is finally undone by Hayden Walsh. Joel Wilson is asked to change his decision to OUT!

OUT! The decision is overturned. Flighted delivery, landing full and around middle, Starc sits down on one knee for the sweep shot but fails to connect cleanly. He is hit on the back leg, they appeal and appeal and appeal but the umpire remains unmoved. The bowler and the keeper manage to convince Kieron Pollard who goes for the DRS. The Ultra Edge shows no spike and the Ball Tracker indicates THREE REDS. The stand has been broken and Australia are 96 for 7.
Another googly, full and on middle, Wade plays late and guides it to the left of short third man for one.
Loopy and full around leg, a googly, Wade keeps it out off his front foot to mid-wicket.
The 50-run stand comes up! A much-needed one for Australia. Fuller in length and sliding down the leg side, Wade helps it to fine leg for one.
Cottrell digs in a short ball on off, Starc stands back and pulls it to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Spears in a fuller length ball on off, Starc chooses to hang on the back foot as he keeps it out to short mid-wicket.
Too full in length and on middle, Wade tries to flick but it takes the leading edge and goes in the gap at covers. They cross for a run.
Back of a length ball on off, Wade defends it from the back foot to point.
Good length ball landing on middle and straightening a bit, Wade brings his bat down and defends it back.
An absolute peach to end the over. This one is flighted around off and Starc looks to block it but the wrong one turns away and beats the outside edge of Starc's bat.
A tad bit short on the legs, Wade flicks it off the back foot towards square leg for one.
A touch flatter on middle but spinning in, Wade gives himself room and plays it nicely towards point. Not in the gap though.
Low full toss on off, Wade misses out as he drives it gently to covers.
Tossed up on middle, Wade defends it off the front foot.
Pushed wide on a length, Wade lets it through.
Length ball into the hips, Wade tucks it off the back foot towards mid-wicket for a single.
WIDE! Short bouncer, a bit too short, Wade ducks down and a wide is called.
Slightly pitched up into the channel, Wade lets it through.
FOUR! That was skilful from Wade, length ball around off but Wade just opens the face of the bat at the very last second and nudges it very fine and into the fence at third man.
Pacy short ball outside off, Wade tries to slash it over third man but gets beaten.
Back of a length on off, Wade pushes it off the back foot to the point region.
Pitched up around off, a cracking cover drive from Wade but finds the fielder.
WIDE! Drifting way down leg and Wade lets it go. Wided.
Fuller delivery around leg stump, Starc looks to sweep hard but misses to get hit onto the pads. Appeal from the bowler but the umpire shakes his head.
This one is bowled slower and is tossed up around off, Starc waits for it and defends it well.
Flighted delivery on the stumps, Wade leans forward and pushes it to long on for one.
A touch shorter on leg stump, Wade gets back in his crease and gently nudges it towards square leg.
Tossed up on off, watchfully blocked out by Wade.
Pushed through nicely just outside off, Wade tries to cut away from his body but gets beaten.
Hayden Walsh replaces Akeal in the attack. 0/9 in his 3 overs so far.
Length ball around middle and leg, pushed gently to mid on.
Pitched up this time on leg, Starc drives it straight to mid on.
Back of a length outside off, Wade guides it down to third man off his back foot for a single.
Length ball on middle and leg, Wade blocks it out.
Shorter one on middle, Wade pulls it hard but straight to the fielder.
Length ball, flicked to deep mid-wicket for a couple.
Sheldon Cottrell is into the attack. 2-1-2-1 are his figures so far.
Tossed up around off, watchfully kept out by Starc.
A bit shorter on off, pushed off the back foot to the cover region.
WIDE! Tried to bowl this one a bit flatter but it drifts down leg. Starc leaves it alone and a wide is called.
A bit flatter around off and Starc covers the line and defends it to the off side.
Flighted delivery on middle, watchfully blocked out by Starc.
Tossed up around off but a bit quicker, Starc looks to block but gets beaten and the ball flicks his back pad. A faint appeal but turned down.
Tossed up on off, played down to long on by Wade for a single.
In the channel outside off, left alone. Two boundaries from the over and this partnership is settling down nicely for Australia.

FOUR! Smashed down the ground! Joseph goes fuller this time and lands it on off, Starc brings down a straight bat and smacks it straight past the bowler for a boundary. Australia have gone past their previous lowest total in ODIs.
A length ball on off, angling away, Starc shoulders arms.

FOUR! Starc gets hold of this one and it goes like a tracer bullet. Short in length and close to off, this time Starc rides the bounce and plays a cracking pull shot over mid-wicket. Bang. The stand moves to 29 runs.
Swing and a miss! Short in length and outside off, once again good pace from Joseph, Starc takes on the challenge to pull it but it bounces over his blade.
Beaten! Back of a length ball close to off, angling away with good pace and bounce, Starc feels for it from the back foot and gets beaten.

Shout for an lbw! The impact is an issue again. Full and outside off, spinning in, Wade tries to swipe it across the line but misses. He is struck on the pads, they appeal but the umpire shakes his head.
Short leg comes in.
Slower one, full and flighted on off, Wade leans forward and defends it to mid-wicket.
FOUR! Some innovations will bring runs for Australia! Flighted delivery, full and outside off, Wade reverse sweeps it wide of first slip for a boundary.
A touch flatter and quicker through the air, short on off, Starc goes back and works it with the spin to deep square leg for a run.
Floated ball, around off and spinning in, Starc defends it to the off side.
Too full in length on off, Wade steps down and forces it to long on for a single.
Edgy! Width on offer outside off, Wade goes for an expansive cover drive but ends up edging it down to third man for a run.
A touch short and on off, angling away, Wade goes on his toes and taps it down to point.
Play and a miss! Good pace from Alzarri Joseph. He hurls across a length delivery wide outside off, Wade flashes and misses.
Shortish and on middle, Starc tries to defend but it takes the inner half and goes in front of square leg. They cross.
Back of a length ball outside off, punched off the back foot on the off side but straight to the cover fielder.
In the channel outside off, Starc allows it through to the keeper.
Bowling change. Alzarri Joseph comes back into the attack. He has figures of, 1/12 in 3 overs so far.
Presses forward to a full ball and drives it down to long off for a single.

Review for LBW by Australia. Mitchell Starc has been given OUT by the onfield umpire but he has reviewed it straightaway. No bat involved. Ball Tracking shows that the impact is outside off and hence the decision is overturned. Big relief for the Aussies and Starc lives to fight on.

NOT OUT! Tossed up ball landing full outside off and spinning back in, Starc goes down to slog sweep but misses and is hit on the back thigh. They appeal and the finger goes up. Starc takes the DRS. There is no bat involved, confirms the Ultra Edge while the Ball Tracker shows that the impact is outside the line of the off stump. Starc will continue.
Tossed up ball around off, Starc drives it straight back and it collides with the stumps at the other end.
That is defended solidly off the front foot.
Too full and on off, Starc hammers it down to long on where Cottrell fumbles and allows the second run.

Howzzat? The umpire is not interested. Akeal puts a lot of revs on the ball, Starc tries to defend but it beats the inside edge and lobs off the pads of the keeper. Holder catches it reacting from first slip. They appeal but nothing from the umpire. The square leg umpire has called it a no ball, as West Indies had one extra fielder outside the ring. Free Hit coming up and for safety reasons, the forward short leg fielder will have to move out. So, for this delivery, West Indies will have 10 players on the ground.
Aerial but safe! Flatter ball, short and on off, Wade goes back and hits it in the air. There is no mid on in place and hence a run.
Fullish and outside off, Wade drives it down to long off and picks up a run.
Very full in length and outside off, Starc drags it down off the toe end of his bat to long on for a single.
Wide! Tossed up ball wide down the leg side, Starc moves away from the line and lets it be.
A touch short and on middle, Starc moves back and hits it to long leg for two.
Goes back and flicks it on the leg side, finds backward square leg.
Gets beaten! Flatter leg spinner again, around off and on the shorter side too, Starc goes back to defend but it whizzes past the outside edge.
Flatter leg spinner outside off, on the shorter side, Starc punches it to point.
On a length around middle, Wade gives himself room and plays it wide of long on for a couple.
Slightly tossed up on middle and watchfully kept out by Wade.
Flatter delivery around middle, Wade tucks it off the back foot to square leg.
WIDE! Drifting down leg again and Wade lets it go. Wide signalled. 50 up for Australia!
Leg Bye! A bit short on middle, Starc looks to sweep but the ball pops up of his pads over leg slip and the batsmen get a leg bye.
Close again! Tosses this one on a length outside off, Starc looks to push it towards covers but the spin makes the ball go through the gate but the ball misses the stumps.
WIDE! A bit shorter, drifting down leg, Starc looks to flick but misses. Wided.
Darted in on middle, Starc blocks it out nicely.

Drinks break! 47 for 6 and Australia are staring down the barrel. It has been some exceptional bowling from West Indies, especially Akeal Hosein. Once again Australia have been exposed by a spinner and they will require a miracle from here to reach a competitive score.
Shorter delivery, played off the back foot towards mid-wicket.

WADE IS SAFE! Tossed up ball landing full around off and turning towards the leg stump, Wade goes down and across to play the sweep shot but misses. The keeper is quick to take the bails off and appeals. It has been referred upstairs and the replays find that Wade has some part of his boot inside the crease. The third umpire also checks for caught behind but there is a flat line on the Ultra Edge.

Shout for a stumping! The square leg umpire takes it upstairs. The third umpire first checks for the stumping but there is some part of Wade's boot planted in. He further goes on to check for caught behind. There is nothing on the Ultra Edge. Wade is safe.
Full toss on the legs, driven down to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Flighted delivery around leg, turning away, watchfully kept out by Starc.
Good length on middle, blocked out by Starc.
Tossed up on off, pushed to the cover region.
Fuller this time on middle, Wade tries to counter with a sweep but misses the ball. He is hit on his wrists. End of an incredible over, two runs and two wickets off it.
Tossed up around off, Starc leans into his cover drive and gets a run after finding the gap.
Mitchell Starc is the new batsman. Not sure he has ever batted this early in the innings. A slip, short leg and leg slip in place. Pollard is in the attacking mood.

OUT! TIMBER! This is just classical spin bowling by Akeal Hosein. He is ripping through this Australian line-up now. Flighted delivery on middle, drifting in but then at the last moment turns away and bamboozles Turner who tries to block it by getting forward. The ball lands, grips and spins past his bat to shatter the stumps. West Indies are cock-a-hoop!
Leg Bye! Drifting onto the pads, Wade tries to flick but it's off the pads and down to short fine leg for a single.

OUT! CAUGHT! Akeal Hosein strikes again! Nicely tossed up delivery, just outside off, allowing the ball to spin and makes Henriques play at it. Henriques leans forward but is undone by the turn and gets the outside edge to first slip where Holder takes a sharp catch. Australia are in tatters!
Commentary.Howout: c Jason Holder b Akeal Hosein

Commentary.Commentary: Matthew Wade arrives in the middle. In a recent interview, he had talked about making full use of the opportunity he is getting in the ODI team and he is aware that it has come because Finch isn't fit. Can he bail Australia out?
Darted in on off, cut straight to point.
Flighted delivery on the stumps, watchfully blocked out.
Full and straight again, blocked past the bowler for one.
SAFE! Flighted delivery around middle, Turner flicks it slightly in the air but past Pollard at mid-wicket for a single.
Shorter one on middle stump, Henriques makes room and pulls this one down to deep square leg for one.
Tossed up on middle, Henriques gets behind the line of the ball to block it.
Full and straight, driven straight to covers.
Hayden Walsh is into the attack now. He has been in great form from the time Australia have stepped on West Indies' soil.
A bit short around off, turning away, Ashton hits it in the air but it doesn't carry to cover-point.
Ashton Turner is the new batsman. He played very well for his 49 in the first ODI and had a century stand with Carey. Can he do something similar with Moises Henriques?

OUT! TIMBER! Dream delivery by Akeal Hosein this time. Gives it air just around off, Carey looks to hit this one over long on but gets beaten by the flight and pace of the ball as it goes through the gate and crashes into the stumps. Australia are in big, big trouble now.
Length ball, darted in, Carey sweeps it off one knee straight to square leg.
Full and straight, swept away to square leg.
Short and wide, played off the back foot to deep point for a single.
Short leg in place.
Slightly tossed up around off, blocked nicely by Henriques.
TWO WIDES! Similar delivery, this time Carey misses the flick but the ball goes past the keeper to short fine leg and the batsmen cross.
WIDE! Flatter one on leg, spins in and strays down the leg side. Wided.
Powerplay 2 time. A maximum of 4 fielders are now allowed outside the ring till the 40th over. There is a bowling change too, Akeal Hosein is into the attack.
Bowling change. Akeal Hosein comes in.
Smashed away! Short in length and wide outside off, Alex cuts it firmly and it goes off the outer half to deep backward point. Third man is square, so only a run.
Back of a length ball on middle and off, Carey goes on the back foot and defends it down safely.

A bit short and on off, Carey opens the face of his bat and dabs it to the right of backward point. The fielder there runs across and then dives to take the pace off the ball. After that, the first slip fielder picks up the ball.
Good length ball on off, Carey gets on the front foot and defends it towards backward point.
Slapped away! Short in length and wide outside off, Alex slaps it over cover-point and collects a brace.
Angles away a length ball outside off, Carey presses forward and pushes it to the left of point.
A delivery on a driving length outside off, seaming away, Henriques watches it closely and then leaves it alone.
Good length delivery outside off, shaping away, Moises has nothing to do with it.
Angling in, on a length around off, Moises defends it from the back foot.

That's a lovely shot and a good effort in the field by Cottrell. Fuller in length and on middle, Carey flicks it through the gap at mid-wicket. Sheldon chases it and puts an early dive as he pulls it back in. The ball again starts to roll towards the fence but Cottrell recovers quickly from his dive and picks it up. Saves one run.
Pushes a length ball to covers and scampers across to the other end.
A length ball on off, the batsman has just watchfully blocked this out.

FOUR! Uppish and just over the leaping cover fielder. Full and outside off, Carey leans forward and chips his drive over covers. It races away and then starts to slow down as it approaches the fence. Akeal Hosein chases and dives near the fence to pull it back. The onfield umpire gets it checked upstairs and finds that Akeal's elbow has touched the rope when he is in contact with the ball. A boundary is given.
That is punched off the back foot but straight to the fielder at covers.
Another delivery is angled away from the left-hander, on a length and zipping away, Carey shoulders arms.
The line is straight, a length ball, Alex works it off his pads to mid-wicket.
Second slip is going in.
Good length delivery angling away from the batsman, outside off, Carey makes a leave.
Skipper Alex Carey is in next.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! That's a big breakthrough for West Indies and their players are running in celebration. Mitchell Marsh has been a nuisance for them with the bat on this tour and the hosts are delighted to see his back so early. This is Test-match line and length from Holder, he serves it on a length around off, angling in and Marsh has to play the line. But the ball nips away slightly to take the outside edge. Shai Hope takes another catch and Australia are three down now.
Commentary.Howout: c Shai Hope b Jason Holder

Commentary.Commentary: Angling in, Marsh clips it to deep square leg for a single.
Aerial but safe! On a length and outside off, holding up a bit, Marsh chips his drive over cover and takes a couple.
Moises Henriques walks in next at number 4.

OUT! One shot too many from Josh Philippe. West Indies chalked out a plan, the trap was laid by keeping a deep fielder on the leg side and Josh walked into it. Alzarri Joseph dishes out a shortish length ball around off and the propensity of Josh Philippe to play the pull shot has cost him. He doesn't find the middle of the bat and it balloons in the air towards deep square leg. Evin Lewis is planted there strategically, he gets underneath it and makes no mistake.
Commentary.Howout: c Evin Lewis b Alzarri Joseph

Commentary.Commentary: In the air...safe! Full and on middle, stopping a bit onto the batsman, Josh checks his on drive and chips it in the air. It dies down quickly before rolling to mid on.
Fuller and around off, Josh Philippe isn't entirely forward as he defends it with a dead straight blade.
Meanwhile, Sheldon Cottrell has returned on the field.
Good length ball on off, angling in, Philippe is watchful as he blocks it from the crease.
Full in length and on off, Mitchell walks across and defends it back to the bowler.

FOUR! Glorious! That's the shot of a batsman in prime form. Holder bowls it fuller and around off, Marsh shows the full face of his bat and unfurls a sumptuous off drive. Beats mid off and races away.
Fuller in length and on off, Marsh inside edges his attempted flick shot to mid-wicket. The fielder there fumbles but it rolls towards mid on. No run taken.
Fuller in length and on off, angling in at 126 kph, Marsh presents a straight bat and defends it back without much followthrough.
Catch it is the shout...it falls safely! Short in length and around off, Marsh is early with his pull shot and misses. It lobs off his shoulders and drops in front of the charging first slip fielder.
Back of a length ball on off, Marsh goes on the back foot and punches it with an angled bat to point.
FOUR! Good length delivery around off, some extra bounce available, Philippe swivels on the back foot and heaves it over mid-wicket for a boundary. Nice shot to close the over.
Shortish and outside off, Josh goes on his toes and taps it down to backward point.
Around off on a length, that is defended solidly off the front foot.

Back of a length delivery outside off, Mash punches it to cover-point. Nicholas Pooran collects the ball, finds Philippe outside the crease and has a shy at the bowler's end. Josh though is in by then. It's a direct hit, taking the ball away from mid on and the batsmen take a run.
Play and a miss! Alzarri Joseph delivers it short and wide outside off, Marsh tries to slam it over point but the ball bounces over his bat.
Starts his spell with a shortish ball outside off, Marsh rocks back to play the square cut but gets it away off the bottom edge.
Alzarri Joseph is into the attack, Sheldon Cottrell is off the field.
Good length ball on off, it's defended off the back foot.

FOUR! Uppish but safe! Fuller in length and on middle, Josh presents the full face of the bat and drives it aerially back past the bowler and his partner. Holder sticks his right hand out but it's too far from him. The ball races down the ground, Alzarri Joseph gives it the chase, tries to pull it back in and in the process collides with the advertising board. No harm done though. The onfield umpire gets it checked upstairs and the third umpire finds that Alzarri Joseph's hands were in contact with the rope. Boundary signalled.
Another length ball is angled in around middle, it's defensively pushed down to mid on.
FOUR! Cracking shot! Holder hurls in a short delivery around off, angling in, Philippe hangs on the back foot and pulls it powerfully in front of square leg for a boundary, first of the match.
Fuller in length and close to off, much better line, Philippe gets forward and drives it down the ground. Finds mid off.
Good length ball on middle, Philippe gets forward and across before pushing it with the angle of the bowler to mid-wicket.
Drops it on a length around leg, shaping down, Mitchell fails to flick and it clips his pads on its way to the keeper. A muted appeal dies down quickly.
Wide! Cottrell will have to re-bowl this as well. Short but down the leg side, shaping further down, Marsh stays back and lets it be.
Called a dead ball. Sheldon Cottrell might have been looking for a slower one but it slipped out of his hands as he was about to deliver. Reload.
A length ball on leg, Marsh works it off his pads to square leg.
Cottrell goes short but the line is on middle and leg, it's pulled behind square leg fo a single.
Cottrell pulls his length back and delivers it outside off, Josh goes on the back foot and punches it to covers.
Serves it full and on middle, Philippe brings down a straight bat and pushes it down to mid on.
Beaten all ends up! A yorker from Sheldon Cottrell, swinging in the air and landing outside off, Philippe tries to drive but misses.
A length ball is angled around off, Marsh stays back and defends it to mid-wicket.
Fractionally short and on off, once again Philippe favours staying on the back foot and nudges it behind square leg for one.
This one is on a driving length outside off, Josh decides to remain on the back foot as he covers his stumps and allows it through.
First runs off the bat! Slightly short in length and on off, Philippe gets across and works it in front of square leg for a couple of runs.
Back of a length ball on top of off, Josh gets behind the line and defends it back from the crease.
Good length delivery in the channel outside off, a hint of inward movement, Philippe covers everything before making a leave.
Who will bowl from the other end? It is going to be Jason Holder to partner with Cottrell. Two slips in place.
Cottrell pitches it up and wide outside off, Marsh tries driving but it takes the inner part of his bat and rolls back to the bowler. A good first over by Cottrell.
A juicy full toss to greet the new batsman, Marsh though pushes it from the back foot to covers. Fails to make any use of the gift.
The batsman in red-hot form, Mitchell Marsh, is the new batsman.

OUT! Early success for West Indies and here comes the trademark salute from Sheldon Cottrell. A poor shot selection from McDermott and he bags a duck. First delivery from Sheldon in the region outside off, it's short and wide, Ben flashes his bat at it and gets a thick outside edge straight to Shai Hope. A disappointed Ben McDermott is back in the hut.
Commentary.Howout: c Shai Hope b Sheldon Cottrell

Commentary.Commentary: Awkward bounce from a length around leg, Ben tries to negotiate but fails and is hit on the body.
Slightly short in length and on middle and leg, Philippe stays back to work it on the leg side. He misses and it goes off thigh pad to fine leg for a leg bye.
Hint of swing for Cottrell. He delivers it full and on middle, Josh flicks it on the leg side but finds the short mid-wicket fielder.

It's time to get going! The players are on the ground. Josh Philippe and Ben McDermott are the Aussie openers. Sheldon Cottrell will bowl with the first new ball. The players take a knee first up and now we are ready to play. Here we go...

Pitch report - No water has been added to the surface. There are patches of green grass on the deck along with dry grass. There will be variable bounce and this pitch is going to be very tough for batting.
JUST IN - Josh Hazlewood is not feeling well and Wes Agar has been allowed to take his place in the XI.

Right! Let's focus on the game at hand. The series is still wide open with Australia having the upper hand. For West Indies, it's not just about winning the next two matches but also plucking 20 CWC points that are up for grabs. If they do that, the hosts will shoot up from 9th and go level with Australia on the points table. Plenty riding on this and the next game.

Moving on, as you must be already aware that all the RT-PCR tests conducted came negative. It's a piece of very good and relieving news but at the same time, a gentle reminder to all of us that we're not yet free from the clutches of Covid-19 and all the necessary precautions have to be taken.

West Indies (Playing XI) - Evin Lewis, Shai Hope (WK) (In for Shimron Hetmyer), Darren Bravo, Jason Mohammed, Nicholas Pooran, Kieron Pollard (C), Jason Holder, Hayden Walsh, Sheldon Cottrell, Alzarri Joseph, Akeal Hosein.

Australia (Playing XI) - Josh Philippe, Ben McDermott, Mitchell Marsh, Moises Henriques, Alex Carey (WK/C), Ashton Turner, Matthew Wade, Mitchell Starc, Riley Meredith (In for Wes Agar), Adam Zampa, Josh Hazlewood.

Take 2! And first things first. There won't be any start from scratch in the second ODI. The match will RESUME from the point we left it two days back due to unfortunate circumstances. So, as it has been flashing on the scorecard all day, Australia will bat first, and both teams will continue with the already announced XIs. For your convenience, so that you don't have to scroll all the way down, our next updates will carry the information regarding the Playing XIs of Australia and West Indies. Be with us...

What can we say now? STUMPS ON DAY 1! Ha ha ha. Join us back at 2.30 pm local then (1830 GMT)! We should have a fair idea about what is the final call about the toss by then. The good thing is that after that one positive case, everyone else in both squads has returned negative Covid tests. So the match should happen for sure. Fingers crossed.

However, Australia have problems. As per the rule, once the toss has happened, you are supposed to play with the same lineups which were announced at that time. West Indies are ready to abide by the rules but Australia want a fresh toss, so that they can have a new lineup, because the one announced was as per the conditions and the pitch on Thursday. So they have raised the matter to the ICC and we all await what will be the final decision. Of course, rules are rules but food for thought for the ICC? Since neither team got onto the field, would there be any issue in having a new toss? What if, you selected a team based on specific conditions and the next day, conditions change? Will be interesting to see ICC's take on this.

MATCH TO RESUME! Of course, not now. But at the time the third ODI was originally scheduled. So it was on Saturday, 24th July, 2021, at 2.30 pm local (1830 GMT). The date and time are the same but this will now be considered as the second ODI. The boards have agreed to play another game on Monday, 26th July, at 2.30 pm local (1830 GMT). Australia of course, won't have any problems but West Indies might, because they are slotted to play Pakistan the very next day!

Very unfortunate and surprising to say the least! The toss was done and play was about to start but a last-minute positive Covid-19 Test has seen the game to be suspended and thrown the remainder of the series into jeoprady. This shows how uncertain times are currently and we hope wherever you are watching, you are taking the right precautions and care to fight this battle against Covid-19. Let's hope everyone is safe and the person affected is not too adversely affected as that is the priority. We hope to see you soon. Till then, goodbye and take care!

UPDATE 1510 local (1910 GMT) - The official statement from Cricket West Indies ''The second  ODI between West Indies and Australia has been postponed due a positive Covid-19 test result from a non-playing member of the West Indies team. This decision was taken after the toss at Kensington Oval once the result was known due to the Covid-19 protocols. All members of both teams and match officials will be retested today. A decision on when the match will replayed will be made at a later date once the test results are known.''

UPDATE 1448 Local (1848 GMT) - PLAY POSTPONED! This is something no one expected! It has come out of the blue if we are being honest! In these uncertain times, there has been a positive Covid-19 Test in the bubble and the game has been POSTPONED!
Not the news we would have liked to start the day. The start of the game will be delayed by a little due to some operational issues.

PITCH REPORT - Darren Ganga is the pitch master for the day. Ganga says it is a glorious afternoon and tells there is a 30 percent chance of rain. Ganga says the straighter boundary is bigger. Ganga says that the wicket got slower. Darren Ganga says this pitch is light brown in color and says it is very dry. Tells the grass covering is patchy and batting will be tougher. He feels the bowlers will take advantage.

West Indies skipper, Kieron Pollard says that they just need to fix what went wrong. Pollard admits their batting was the problem and hopes to correct it and improve the situation. Pollard says today is one of the biggest game and says they have had a lot of discussions and hopes to do the business today. Pollard informs Hetmyer misses out and Hope comes back from injury.

Australia skipper, Alex Carey says they will elect to bat first, as the pitch looks similar to the first game. Also says, they are happy to start the ODI series with a victory and would look to continue with the same momentum. Ends by saying there is one change, Riley Meredith comes in place of Wes Agar.

West Indies (PLAYING XI) - Evin Lewis, Shai Hope (WK) (IN PLACE OF SHIMRON HETMYER) , Darren Bravo, Jason Mohammed, Nicholas Pooran, Kieron Pollard (C), Jason Holder, Hayden Walsh, Sheldon Cottrell, Alzarri Joseph, Akeal Hosein.

Australia (PLAYING XI) - Josh Philippe, Ben McDermott, Mitchell Marsh, Moises Henriques, Alex Carey (WK/C), Ashton Turner, Matthew Wade, Mitchell Starc, Riley Meredith (IN PLACE OF WES AGAR), Adam Zampa, Josh Hazlewood.
TOSS - The coin goes up and lands in the favour of Australia. They opt to bat first.

Hello and welcome to the second ODI between West Indies and Australia. The hosts capitulated with the bat and failed to get even close to Australia's target. Pollard and co. Will look to put on a much improved showing with the bat this time around. It was a very good performance from the visitors and they will be eyeing to repeat it and avenge for the T20I series loss by taking an unassailable lead tonight. Starc finding his mojo back would be the biggest boost for Australia. Can the hosts fight back to level the series or will Australia wrap it up? Stay tuned for toss and further updates.
